//: Copy to config.json and fill in. config.json is gitignored, so never commit it.
//content: The content sections (event, game, kiosk, stream, sponsors, awards.list, rundown, accessibility) only SEED the first run: the desk's Event setup group and the Judge Advisor's awards page edit them live, and those edits land in data/event-content.json, which overrides this file from then on. Credentials and the camera list live only here.

event.//key: TBA event key. CalGames 2026 is expected to be 2026cacg. Confirm on thebluealliance.com before the event.
event.//name: Event name as it appears in titles, following the official FIRST channel convention: 'Qualification 1 - CalGames', 'Match 1 (R1) - CalGames', 'Final Tiebreaker - CalGames'. Livestreams read '2026 CalGames - Day 1'.
event.name: CalGames
event.//resultsUrl: Linked in every video description. Blank omits the line.

game.//: Bonus RP thresholds. Off-season events move these, and the 2026 REBUILT numbers were still being argued over while this was built. They travel on the state snapshot, so changing one here changes the reducer, every badge, and the talent view together. Defaults below match the REBUILT constants in apps/core/src/types.ts.

kiosk.//fieldStreamUrl: Field picture for pit monitors at /s/watch. A YouTube live URL, an MJPEG stream off a capture box, or any video URL a browser plays. Blank draws the CalGames backdrop instead. Served to the open pit-monitor pages through /api/urls, so never point it at anything you would not put on a projector.

publish.//enabled: Master switch. Nothing uploads while this is false.
publish.//mode: deferred | trickle | live. Keep deferred during competition: the live stream must never compete with an upload for the venue uplink. Measure the uplink on Friday before changing this.
publish.//autoQueuePractice: Practice matches queue automatically too ('Practice 3 - CalGames'). They upload but never link on TBA, which has no keys for practice. Set false to keep Friday load-in off the channel; queueing one by hand from the desk always works regardless.
publish.//autoQueueArcade: Each finished arcade set queues as its own segment video, titled like 'Arcade Winners Semifinal (Smash)', from the set's start to when it ended.
publish.//privacy: Videos upload unlisted and flip to public only once TBA linking succeeds, so a failed link never leaves an orphan video with no context.
publish.//playlists: YouTube playlist IDs (PL...). Leave blank to skip playlist insertion.
publish.//credit: Closing lines of every description, mirroring the official channel's layout. FIRST's own videos end '(c) 2026 FIRST Robotics Competition' (that is theirs to claim). CalGames is a WRRF off-season event, so these default to WRRF.
publish.credit: Uploaded by the CalGames Content Desk

recording.//: What the rolling recorder captures when the desk is launched with --record. One entry per feed: role 'program' is the composited broadcast (what uploads are cut from), role 'iso' is a raw camera (replay source only). 'input' is the ffmpeg input arguments as an array. A malformed entry is skipped with a warning at startup, never a crash. --test-sources ignores this list and records color bars instead.

audio.//: House audio: the room's PA, and only the room's PA. Nothing here can reach the stream. The two-bus rule in docs/06 is a cable, not a setting, and this is a control surface for the machine that already had the music on it.
audio.//enabled: Walk-up clips and stingers work with this on and nothing else configured: they play off this disk, with no internet and no account.
audio.//spotify: Optional background playlist. Requires a Spotify PREMIUM account (remote control does not work on free), and read the licensing note in docs/06 before using it at a public event.
audio.//clientId: From developer.spotify.com/dashboard. Not a secret: PKCE needs none.
audio.//refreshToken: Run: npm run auth:spotify. Expires six months after it is minted, used or not.
audio.//deviceName: The name the music machine's Spotify shows under Connect. Blank drives whatever device is already active.

sponsors.//: Who paid for this. Tier decides how often a sponsor comes round in the rotation (title 3x, major 2x, supporting 1x), never how big it is drawn.
sponsors.//report: GET /api/sponsors?report=1 gives pasteable text: appearances and seconds on screen per sponsor, counted from the broadcast itself.
sponsors.//logo: Optional path under /media, e.g. /media/sponsors/acme.png. The name is always drawn, so a missing logo is not a broken card.

setup.//: The settings code for /s/setup, where the content half of this file (event, sponsors, run of show, thresholds, accessibility) is edited live by the content lead. Ships as 4567; change it for the event. Not the desk PIN, not the awards code. Explicitly empty = the desk PIN covers settings. Env var SETUP_PIN overrides.

awards.//: The judged awards, with the definition the GA reads on air while the plate is up. The desk shows title+definition first and reveals the winner on a second press; the winner never enters any feed until that press.
awards.//pin: The Judge Advisor's code, NOT the desk PIN. Ships as 1357; change it for the event. The awards panel locks behind it: the JA loads winners from /s/awards all day (that page needs only this code), and the desk crew cannot see, type, or reveal a winner until the JA hands this code over before the ceremony. Explicitly empty = no separate tier, desk PIN covers awards. Env var JA_PIN overrides.
awards.//list: The ceremony, in the order it is presented. "day" groups the two ceremonies, and the Judge Advisor page and the desk panel both group by it. "description" is the committee's full definition: what the GA reads aloud and what the projected deck shows. "blurb" is the single line the BROADCAST plate shows, because a 600 character paragraph on a 1080 frame is a wall nobody in the hall reads; leave it blank and the plate falls back to the description's first sentence.

list.title: Directors' Award
list.blurb: From the WRRF Board, for outstanding service to the regional robotics community.
list.description: The Director's Award is presented by the WRRF Board of Directors to a person, organization, company, volunteer, or team that has contributed significantly to the mission of the Western Region Robotics Forum as a whole, in any outstanding way. It is WRRF's way of saying thank you to those who make the regional robotics community possible.

list.title: Volunteer of the Year Award
list.blurb: For the volunteer whose sustained work and gracious professionalism set the standard.
list.description: CalGames is very grateful to have many dedicated, supportive volunteers behind all its competitions, lending their time, effort, and expertise to make those events successful. This award recognizes one such individual who sets the standard: sustained contribution to CalGames, reliability in a lead or critical role, and gracious professionalism toward teams and fellow volunteers.

list.title: Mentor of the Year Award
list.blurb: For a mentor whose guidance shapes both their students and the wider community.
list.description: A Mentor earns the Mentor of the Year Award with support from a team. An effective and successful mentoring relationship is characterized by mutual respect, trust, understanding, and empathy. Good Mentors share life experiences and wisdom, as well as technical, non-technical, and leadership expertise. They are good listeners, good observers, and good problem-solvers. They make efforts to know, accept, and respect the goals and interests of all students and also contribute to the wider robotics community.

list.title: Founders' Award
list.blurb: CalGames' highest honor: a team's sustained impact beyond the field, down, across and up.
list.description: The Founders' Award is CalGames' highest recognition of a team's impact beyond the field. This award honors outstanding, sustained effort in promoting and celebrating STEM: passing it DOWN to younger students, ACROSS to peer teams and the community, and UP to alumni, adults, and seniors. The team embodies the goal of inspiring respect and honor for science and technology while encouraging today's youth to become leaders in entrepreneurship, engineering, science, and technology. The award honors the accomplishments and measured successes that the team has sustained over the past three years.

list.title: Rookie Inspiration Award
list.blurb: For a rookie team already inspiring its community and building to last.
list.description: The Rookie Inspiration Award recognizes a team who may be new to the competition but already enthusiastically demonstrates the WRRF's mission of inspiring their community. They have begun forging partnerships, building sustainable processes, and establishing a lasting team foundation. Judges are impressed by this team's success and look forward to their bright future.

list.title: Imagery Award
list.blurb: For the team whose robot, pit, uniforms and media all tell one clear story.
list.description: The Imagery Award highlights a team which builds a cohesive brand by integrating the design of their robot with their uniforms, pit, media and more. Imagery is more than looking good: this team executes a documented plan that leverages their identity to generate awareness and build interest in the team, its robot, and among students, sponsors, and the community.

list.title: Highest Seeded Rookie Award
list.blurb: To the rookie team ranked highest at the end of qualification matches.
list.description: The Highest Seeded Rookie Award is presented to the Rookie team with the highest ranking at the end of qualification matches.

list.title: Autonomous and Controls Award
list.blurb: For software that lets a robot sense, decide and act, on its own and all match long.
list.description: Creating software that enables a robot to sense, decide, and act, both in an autonomous period and throughout a match, is one of the most complex challenges teams face during competition. This award recognizes the team whose students used software engineering practices to design, build, test, and refine effective autonomous routines and match-wide control systems, including sensing and vision, closed-loop control, and driver-assist automation.

list.title: Innovation Award
list.blurb: For a creative approach to a real problem, built this year and proven to work.
list.description: The Innovation Award celebrates creativity with purpose. It recognizes a specific innovative and creative approach, implemented within the past year, to one of the following: (1) a partnership, (2) a manufacturing method, (3) a project other than the game-challenge robot, or (4) the use of technology on the robot. Innovation is judged on the need the team identified, the originality and rigor of their approach, and the level of success they can demonstrate. The team must be able to describe the need, how their approach specifically addresses that need, and how effective it was at its goal.

list.title: Systems Design Award
list.blurb: For a robust, well documented machine and the engineering process behind it.
list.description: The Systems Design Award recognizes an exceptional, robust, and well-documented robot or mechanism design and the engineering process that produced it. Great systems design incorporates components that work together as a whole, requirements that flow from strategy, disciplined prototyping and analysis, quality fabrication, maintainability under competition conditions, and a robot that performs the way its designers intended. Judges consider the design process the team can show, the quality of the machine in front of them, and how the robot performs on the field.

list.title: Entrepreneurship Award
list.blurb: For the team whose planning, management and leadership keep it thriving year on year.
list.description: Fielding a successful and sustainable robotics team is a multi-faceted endeavor requiring engineering, management, and business skills. The Entrepreneurship Award recognizes that it takes extensive organizational management to build robots and compete in competitions year after year. This award highlights a team that has implemented processes that result in successful and sustained team growth and development: project management, financial, documentation, training, and leadership functions.

list.title: Judges' Award
list.blurb: For a team whose story deserves recognition and fits no other award.
list.description: During the competition the Judges may encounter a team whose unique efforts, performance, or dynamics merit recognition: a story that doesn't fit neatly into another award.

slides.//: Recognition and info slides: volunteer thank-yous, SystemCore session times, meeting calls, food-truck hours. The side screens rotate the deck on their own; the desk can take any slide to the program. More get typed at the event and persist to data/slides.json.
slides.//kinds: recognition (thank-you card) or info (announcement card). Shout-outs approved from /s/gp join the deck as a third kind.
slides.//example: { "id": "syscore", "kind": "info", "title": "SystemCore session", "lines": ["Saturday 12:30, Room 201", "Limelight walks through the 2027 controller"] }

rundown.//: The day as a list. The desk manager advances it; nothing advances itself, because a rundown that advances on its own will do it during the one delay nobody predicted.
rundown.//matches: A matches block gives a COUNT, not a duration: the length comes from the pace model measuring real cycle time. A printed 7 minutes against a measured 9 is an hour by the end of the day.
rundown.//audience: What the venue screens call the countdown during this segment, e.g. Matches resume.
rundown.//example: { id: quals-am, label: Qualification matches, kind: matches, matches: 24 }

accessibility.//: What the event actually offers, and where. Shown on the venue screens and the phone page, because the person who needs a quiet room is deciding at 11am in a loud building, from a phone. Leave the list empty if the event offers nothing: showing nothing is honest, and inventing a service is worse than silence.
accessibility.//example: { "label": "Quiet room", "detail": "Room 114, past the pits on the left" }
accessibility.//ask: Who to find. A name and a place beats a policy statement.

nexus.//: FRC Nexus: what the QUEUERS are doing. The only source that knows a match is being called before the field does. Read-only over the internet; nothing to do with the field network.
nexus.//apiKey: From frc.nexus/api. Sent as the Nexus-Api-Key header.
nexus.//eventKey: The Nexus event key, usually the same as event.key. Polling starts when both are set.
nexus.//note: Only useful if the event actually runs its queueing on Nexus. For an event that does not, the timings come back looking authoritative and are not.

startgg.//: Side-tournament bracket from start.gg. Metadata only. Round labels and entrants pre-fill the arcade console; the live score stays operator-authoritative because start.gg lags reality by up to a full round (docs/05-arcade.md).
startgg.//token: Personal access token from start.gg -> Developer Settings. Read scope is enough.
startgg.//eventSlug: The EVENT slug, e.g. tournament/calgames-2026-arcade/event/smash-singles. Polling starts when both fields are set.

youtube.//: Google Cloud project -> OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Desktop app), with the YouTube Data API v3 enabled. Scopes needed: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube. The second covers the flip-to-public after TBA linking, and playlists. `npm run auth:youtube` requests both.
youtube.//refreshToken: Obtained once via the OAuth consent flow. Run `npm run auth:youtube` for the walkthrough.
youtube.//before-the-event: Use WRRF's established, verified channel (a new channel's per-day upload cap is low and separate from API quota). Enable live streaming 24h in advance.

tba.//: Request Trusted API access for the event from The Blue Alliance. They issue an auth id and secret per event.
tba.//scope: We publish video and webcasts only. Cheesy Arena owns match data on TBA. We never call matches/update, rankings/update, awards/update, alliance_selections/update, or team_list/update, since those require the FULL dataset and would delete anything not included.
tba.//readKey: Optional. Read APIv3 key for team names and avatars.

stream.//webcastUrl: The public YouTube live URL. Registered on TBA so the event appears on GameDay. TBA does not ingest video. It only embeds this.
